Who We Are

Film as a Force for Social Change

AfA-SIFF — Art for Advocacy Social Impact Film Forum — is an Abuja-based NGO that harnesses the emotional power of short films to open honest conversations about the social forces shaping Nigerian communities.

We are not a festival. We are a film forum — a deliberate, curated space where stories meet dialogue, and where audiences become advocates.

Registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission as Art for Advocacy Social Impact Film Forum Foundation, we work in close partnership with OtaUmaBen Visuals to bring stories that matter to screens that move people.

📍 Abuja, Nigeria 🎬 Short Film Forum 🏛️ CAC Registered NGO 🏆 Nigeria Youth Futures Fund Partner
Purpose

Mission, Vision & Values

🎯

Our Mission

To use short film as a catalyst for honest social dialogue — bringing communities together around stories that reflect the real pressures, choices and consequences shaping Nigerian life.

🌟

Our Vision

A Nigeria where art drives advocacy — where every community has access to stories that empower, educate, and inspire collective action toward a more just and equitable society.

💡

Our Values

Authenticity in storytelling. Courage in conversation. Inclusivity in audience. Accountability in impact. We believe in art that does not flinch from truth.

AfA-SIFF 2027 — 3rd Edition

"The Cost of Waste" · Abuja, Nigeria · Films, Music, Talks, Impact, Change

🌿 Upcoming
Planned Films & Productions

Proposed 2027 Slate

Nothing is missing. We just waste everything. The 3rd edition explores the environmental, social and economic cost of waste — in all its forms.

🎬 The Shoe Lover

A boy in Abuja's ghetto obsessed with shoes — a story about want, identity, and the cost of chasing what we don't have.

🎬 The Cleaner

A film in development exploring the invisible labor and forgotten lives behind our idea of a clean society.

🎵 The Mother Nature Musical

A special musical rendition exploring humanity's relationship with the natural world — and what we stand to lose.

More film ideas coming · Film submissions open in 2027

AfA-SIFF 2026 — "The Cost of Choice"

Sunday 13th December 2026 · 3PM · Abuja, Nigeria · In partnership with OtaUmaBen Visuals

Panel Discussions

The Conversations We Will Have

Each of the 5 films opens a specific conversation. These are the discussions AfA-SIFF 2026 will facilitate — honest, uncomfortable, and necessary.

01

The Choice to Kill or Protect

When violence becomes survival — exploring the moral cost of choices made under impossible pressure, and what community protection really demands of us.

02

Japa or Stay: The Emigration Dilemma

Brain drain vs. nation building. The personal cost of leaving, and the communal cost of talent departing. What does choosing to leave say about those who stay?

03

Parental Absence & Its Generational Cost

The day a mother leaves — and everything that follows. How parental choices rewrite children's stories, and what healing looks like when it arrives too late.

04

Procrastination as a Life-Altering Choice

"From tomorrow" — the currency we spend most recklessly. A conversation about the choices we keep deferring and the futures we quietly surrender.

05

Identity Under Pressure: Staying Yourself

What does it cost to remain who you are when the world demands you change? A discussion on authenticity, resilience, and the price of staying Still Me.

06

Humanitarian Recognition & Civic Courage

Celebrating those whose choices have made our communities safer, kinder, more just — the annual Humanitarian Honoree recognition at AfA-SIFF 2026.

Special Initiative

My Voice, My Future

"When I Grow Up" — a dual-component Children's Day advocacy event reaching the next generation of storytellers

MY VOICE, MY FUTURE: "When I Grow Up"

Children's Day Initiative · 26 May 2026
📅 26 May 2026
🏫 LEA Primary School, Jabi, Airport Junction, Abuja
👦👧 Primary 5 & 6 Pupils
🤝 OtaUmaBen Visuals

🎤 Component 1: Live Storytelling Competition

Primary 5 and 6 pupils took the stage to tell their own stories — speaking boldly about their dreams, their communities, and the future they want to build.

  • Open to Primary 5 & 6 students
  • Themes: dreams, community, and the future
  • Judged on confidence, originality & message
  • Awards for outstanding young storytellers

🎬 Component 2: Short Advocacy Film Screening

"When I Grow Up" — screened for the pupils to spark honest dialogue about childhood dreams versus lived realities in Abuja's communities.

  • Characters: Emeka, Aisha, Tunde, Adaeze
  • Set across Karimo, Jahi Village, and Jabi
  • Post-screening facilitated discussion
  • Connecting film to lived student experience

Creative Partnership

OtaUmaBen Visuals

OtaUmaBen Visuals

The storytelling engine behind AfA-SIFF. Producing short films that challenge, inspire, and provoke the conversations Nigeria needs to have.

▶ YouTube Channel
The Creative Force Behind Our Stories

Telling Nigeria's Stories with Courage

OtaUmaBen Visuals provides the creative heart of AfA-SIFF — producing short films written, directed, and shot entirely in Nigeria, with stories drawn from the lived realities of Abuja's communities.

In 2026, they completed 7 short films from an ambitious 12-film slate. All 3 films from the 2025 edition are now free to watch on YouTube.

Their commitment earned ONE CALL recognition from the Nigeria Youth Futures Fund — affirming the global resonance of local stories told with integrity.

2025 Panellists

Voices at the Table

Seven distinguished voices who brought expertise, candour and conviction to the maiden edition panel discussions

Nneota Egbe

Legal & Human Rights

Lawyer and human rights advocate with deep expertise in gender-based violence and legal protection frameworks.

Dr. Shola Okpodu

Medical & Public Health

Medical doctor and public health practitioner advocating for access to quality healthcare in underserved communities.

Bunmi Saidi

Child Rights & Education

Child rights advocate and education specialist committed to protecting children's futures through policy and practice.

'Tunbi Olabisi

Media & Communications

Media professional and communications strategist using storytelling to amplify social impact narratives.

Chris Madu

Arts & Culture

Creative director and cultural advocate championing Nigerian arts as a vehicle for social transformation.

Mike Abuh Okoh

Development & Policy

Development practitioner working at the intersection of policy, community development, and social enterprise.

Supt. Samaila Bulus

Law Enforcement

Senior police officer bringing law enforcement perspectives to discussions on safety, justice, and community policing.
